steps.title: A pipe with two ends
text: This is a toy lesson. It teaches you to read the screen before the real lessons start.
A {{term:client}} sends bytes. A {{term:server}} sends the same bytes back. Both run on your computer, over {{term:loopback}}.
This pipe has no lock on it. Later lessons add locks to this same pipe.
Built to show the parts. Do not copy.

steps.title: The client sends first
text: Look at the left lane. The client just put some {{term:byte}}s on the {{term:wire}}.
The arrow shows a name and a byte count. The wire is the path between the two lanes.

steps.title: Read the bytes
text: The panel under the diagram shows the bytes in {{term:hex}}. Each byte takes two characters.
Pick an arrow to see its bytes. The Up and Down keys move between arrows.

steps.title: The server sends them back
text: Now the server answers. It sends the bytes it got back to the client.
Look at the right lane. A new arrow points the other way.

steps.title: Same bytes in, same bytes out
text: Compare the two arrows. The byte counts match.
Pick each arrow and read its hex. The bytes match except the first one: 01 marks the hello and 02 marks the reply.

claims.text: The server returns the same bytes it received, and the engine holds no crypto.
claims.source: src/NetSec.Core/Machine/EchoEngine.cs: the class comment ("before any cryptography exists"), ServerHello (sends the received body back) and ClientReply (compares the reply with the bytes sent)

claims.text: The echo frame is a 1-byte type, a 2-byte length and the body. The hello has type 1 and the reply has type 2, so the reply matches the hello except for the first byte.
claims.source: src/NetSec.Core/Machine/EchoEngine.cs: HelloType = 1, ReplyType = 2, and the frame comment; reader-a15a's run of the lab (PR #57)

steps.title: Every arrow is a trace event
text: Each arrow comes from one {{term:event}} in the {{term:trace}}. The screen draws nothing that the engine did not report.
The status bar shows which event you are on. Free play lists every event in a log.

claims.text: Every engine step emits a trace event, and the screen draws only from trace events.
claims.source: docs/prd.md, Decisions, D4; docs/ux-design.md, Conclusion item 2

steps.title: What Eve sees
text: An {{term:eavesdropper}} named Eve listens on the wire. Switch to the Eavesdropper view.
Eve can read every byte, because nothing is locked. She sees what the client and server see.

claims.text: In the Eavesdropper view, only protected rows turn to noise. Unprotected bytes stay readable.
claims.source: docs/ux-design.md, section 2, moment 2 (Two views of one wire)

steps.title: Locks come next
text: Later lessons add locks to this same pipe. A {{term:key}} turns {{term:plaintext}} into {{term:ciphertext}}.
Then Eve sees noise. Pick lesson 1 on the left rail when you are ready.
